claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a homogeneous single-phase FCC solid solution without pre-existing secondary phases.
High-stress mechanical loading at 300–500°C induces local compositional fluctuations or elemental partitioning in the alloy.
The stress-assisted compositional fluctuations nucleate nanoscale precipitates.
The stress-induced precipitates are brittle intermetallic or sigma phases.
The nanoscale precipitates diminish grain-boundary cohesion.
The nanoscale precipitates diminish cohesion within grains.
Reduced cohesion caused by the precipitates facilitates earlier crack initiation.
Reduced cohesion caused by the precipitates facilitates crack propagation during deformation.
Precipitate-assisted cracking produces a substantial loss of toughness.
Relative to room-temperature tests, samples loaded at 300–500°C under high stress will show reduced toughness.
Relative to room-temperature tests, samples loaded at 300–500°C under high stress will exhibit earlier crack onset.
Nanoscale brittle precipitates will be detectable near fracture zones after high-stress loading at 300–500°C.
At room temperature and lower stress levels, the alloy retains a homogeneous single-phase structure.
At room temperature and lower stress levels, the alloy exhibits ductile behavior.
At temperatures or stresses below the proposed service regime, the alloy maintains its nominal toughness.
Sustained high-stress loading at 300–500°C is representative of demanding engineering service environments applicable to this alloy.
